notes: Sweep 2026-10-31-b for shop-project with the skill: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, model_id matching each tier, head 74112b4 with uncommitted false. skill_hash f2dfc9096cdc68638b654702d080febdc6c942192e04b691cecc45f68e790d1b in every result.json equals common.folder_hash's calculation on the clean idiomatic-elixir/ at 74112b4, so the runs read the text graded here. skills_listed is 209 in every run. Every run read SKILL.md first (#1, or #1, #2 and #7 by cat and sed in haiku-1). Tool calls are numbered once per tool_use id; each transcript repeats some tool_use blocks, and the repeats are not counted. Each Haiku and Sonnet transcript also holds one claude-opus-5-5, in its api-request-shape record, not in a model reply. opus-1 also invoked superpowers:test-driven-development (#13) and wrote its tests before the code.

Rules changed since 0814e8d (git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/): the `for` sentences of "One expression per line, and tabular clauses" and "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else", plus macros.md and processes.md. None of this case's seven rules changed, so all seven and the Formatting bullet are graded to the 2026-10-31 standard: a passing --check-formatted after a file's last edit counts as formatted for Before you finish step 1; a total that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU is clean when its @doc covers it; Map.put/3 on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the forbidden pattern; a code kept as a string and checked against a literal list or map is clean under the atom rule. No run wrote a `for`, so the changed sentences decide nothing here.

Chain fallible steps with `with`: 0 of 5 violated (2026-10-31: 0 of 5). Three runs wrote one-step with blocks with no else and a body that cannot fail: opus-1 lines 72-74, sonnet-1 lines 58-60, 77-79 and 100-102, sonnet-2 lines 65-67. Neither Haiku run wrote a with: haiku-1 lines 63-66 and haiku-2 lines 56-59 are a case on one fallible call that relabels the error, which I graded clean under "An `else` that maps the one error is a `case`, which shows both outcomes in one place.", the standard of 2026-10-31 rate-limiter baseline-haiku-1 lines 131-134 and of the webhook-parser grades. No run wrote a pass-through case, an else or a nested fallible case. Haiku's one not-exercised verdict of 2026-10-31 (haiku-1, an if on membership) has no counterpart here, because both runs now have a fallible lookup.

Per-file formatting check line: met in 1 of 5 (opus-1), the same as 2026-10-31. opus-1 checked the test file alone (#19) before mix test (#20), wrote cart.ex (#21) and checked it (#22, with the test file named too) before compiling. haiku-1: Write of cart.ex (#12), five Edits of the test file (#13-#17), one check on both (#22) after two refused chains. haiku-2: Write and Edit of cart.ex (#5, #6), three Edits of the test file (#7-#9), one check on both (#11) after a refused chain. sonnet-1: a refused python3 heredoc (#4), Write of cart.ex (#5), Edit of the test file (#6), one check on both (#7). sonnet-2: a refused python3 heredoc (#4), Write of cart.ex (#5), two Edits of the test file (#6, #7), a refused chain (#8), mix format on both (#9). In every Haiku and Sonnet run cart.ex was left for the test file before any check. Every check passed on its first run. sonnet-2 is the only run that called mix format, and it moved one line, a wrap after `=` at cart.ex lines 89-90, which the Formatting bullet says stays ("a wrap after `=` or before `|>` is the formatter's own and stays"). The bullet's rewrite half was not exercised.

Other graded rules. Atoms: opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use one parse clause per code string; haiku-1 keeps the string and looks it up in a literal map (lines 14-17, 63); haiku-2 keeps the trimmed, upcased string and checks it against @codes (lines 7, 89). defstruct: bare atoms in all five ([:items, :discount] in three, [:items, :code] in both Haiku runs). Return tuples: atom or tagged-tuple reasons everywhere; opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 raise KeyError on an unpriced SKU and say so in the @doc; sonnet-1 returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}}. Money: integer div in all five; opus-1 rounds the discounted subtotal down, sonnet-2 rounds it halves up, both Haiku runs round the discount halves up, and sonnet-1 rounds the discount down. Naming: domain names throughout; no boolean, get, fetch, size or length functions.

other_violations, all under rules outside this case's list. Clear ones: haiku-2 pipes two steps on one line (cart.ex line 87); haiku-2's test file has three bind-then-== checks (lines 60-61, 65-66, 72-73) and four bare arrange matches (lines 70, 101, 109, 121); haiku-1 spreads a two-entry map over four lines (cart.ex lines 14-17), where the one-line form is 76 characters, the sentence the 2026-10-31 rate-limiter grade applied to sonnet-2's list. Judgment calls, none of which touches a verdict: sonnet-1's prices[sku] (line 101) is listed because the key is required at that point, although check_priced/2 has confirmed it, so the rule's reason for the form (a nil that surfaces later) does not bite; sonnet-1's `context` tests (lines 78-79, 84-85) are the shape 2026-10-31 test-writing opus-1 was graded for, reading the setup's data in the body, here with dot access rather than a match; the "accepts" test names (haiku-1 lines 69 and 73, haiku-2 line 64) are listed as the same shape as the rule's "succeeds with an empty cart", and I found no earlier grade on the word. If the ruling goes the other way on any of these, the entry drops and no verdict moves.

Checked and not listed. sonnet-1's &(not is_map_key(prices, &1)) at line 106: the same shape was clean under the captures rule in 2026-10-30-check-3 order-report sonnet-2 line 133. sonnet-1's multi-line @type t at lines 13-16: it would fit on one line at 86 characters, but a typespec is not a list, map or keyword literal. sonnet-1's check_priced clauses at lines 107-111 on their own lines: the skill's own read_file/1 example lays out short clauses this way, and every `->` entry in the shop-project grades is about a clause too long for one line. The catch-all clauses over a closed set of codes (haiku-2 lines 97 and 100, sonnet-2 lines 109 and 112): the shape-matching rule is about result tuples, and no shop-project grade of any sweep lists them. The wrapped test head at sonnet-2 test lines 84-87: covered by no rule, as in earlier grades. The literal 10 and 90 inside the div calls: the money rule's own examples write the literal. No `## Examples` in the @doc of three runs: not listed in earlier grades. Only haiku-2's test file has a match that can fail without `assert`.
